title: Program evaluation of GLA:D® Germany: a mixed-methods study using the RE-AIM QuEST framework
summary:
Osteoarthritis of the hip and the knee is common and leads to pain, functional disability and reduced quality of life. National and international clinical practice guidelines highlight the importance of non-pharmacological conservative therapy and consistently recommended patient education, exercise therapy and weight management (if overweight or obese) as core management strategies.  In 2013, the Good Life with osteoArthritis from Denmark (GLA:D®) program was initiated in Denmark to translate these recommendations into clinical practice and thus providing patients with hip and/or knee osteoarthritis access to high-quality, evidence-based care. 

GLA:D® consists of three mandatory elements: (1) a two-day education course for physiotherapists in delivering care in accordance with clinical guidelines (2) two educational sessions and (at least) 12 training sessions of 60 minutes each, including neuromuscular exercises, (3) a national GLA:D®-registry for data collection.  

Due to its great success within Denmark, GLA:D® was also implemented in other countries, including Canada, Australia, the Netherlands, Austria, Ireland and Switzerland. In 2022, GLA:D® was introduced in Germany. 

An evaluation of the implementation process in terms of reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation and maintenance as well as possible barriers and facilitators can contribute to the success of GLA:D® Germany.

interventions.name:
Physiotherapists: 
Participation in a two-day education course in delivering care in accordance with clinical guidelines. 

Patients: 
Participation in the GLA:D® program: Two educational sessions and (at least) 12 training sessions of 60 minutes each, including neuromuscular exercises.

Inclusion criteria:
Physiotherapists: 
- Completed professional education

Patients: 
- Diagnosis of hip and/or knee osteoarthritis
Exclusion criteria:
None
